featured_reviews.name: Jyoti Malde
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Avatara for dinner to celebrate our 19th wedding anniversary, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. Their thoughtfully curated 16-course menu, inspired by the Indus Valley and complemented by traditional regional flavors from across India, was truly unique and memorable.
Every course—from the appetizers to the mains and desserts and also Paan ... was beautifully presented and expertly explained by Anirudh, whose warm hospitality added greatly to the evening. Every dish had a surprise twist to it.
We were also surprised with a lovely cake for our anniversary celebration, which made the occasion even more special.
Avatara offers a true gastronomic journey, and I would highly recommend it to anyone who appreciates innovative vegetarian cuisine. A must-visit for food lovers.

featured_reviews.name: shiv '
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a whole, the restaurant was comparable to Michelin Star restaurants we have visited around the world.

The atmosphere in the restaurant was lovely, with gentle music and a violinist playing live music throughout.

We ordered the 16 course menu with wine pairing. Food arrived promptly and the waiters explained each dish and the respective pairings well. The dishes were very thoughtful and creative, adding to the eating experience. Every dish hit the spot.

Overall it seemed really good value for the type of food, especially when compared to Europe, where we are from.

Would recommend visiting, and will be recommending it to everyone I know.

featured_reviews.name: Stanley Vaz
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Avatara, one does not merely dine—one participates in a carefully orchestrated culinary narrative that challenges every preconceived notion of vegetarian cuisine.

From the moment you are seated, the service establishes its quiet authority: attentive without intrusion, polished without pretension. Among the team, Viraj stands out—not with flamboyance, but with a rare, intuitive finesse. His understanding of the menu is not rehearsed, but lived; each course arrives not just as food, but as a story, delivered with precision and warmth.

The cuisine itself is nothing short of revelatory. In a world where vegetarian fare is often relegated to the periphery, Avatara asserts dominance. Every plate is a study in balance—texture, temperature, acidity, and depth all meticulously calibrated. Ingredients are elevated beyond their humble origins, transformed into expressions that are both rooted and avant-garde.

What distinguishes Avatara is its restraint. There is no unnecessary theatrics, no overindulgence in molecular excess. Instead, the kitchen demonstrates confidence—allowing flavours to speak, yet ensuring each bite leaves a lasting impression. It is this quiet mastery that aligns the restaurant with the philosophy of Michelin-starred establishments.

In its totality, Avatara delivers an experience that is immersive, thoughtful, and deeply satisfying. It is not simply one of the finest vegetarian meals—it is one of the finest meals, period.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.name: Mudit Bansal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

Starters we had rasam vada & kancheepuram idli to share - both were well made - vada was soft and so was the idli. The rasam was top notch.
Mains we shared a ghee masala dosa , masala vada and pesarattu -all three were really good .

Service would have been 5* except for a very reluctant server who stood across the table staring at everything but did not take orders or help.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Mashelkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Utasv is a simple and elegant restaurant for family and friends. This is a Veg restaurant. Just because it’s a veg restaurant they have introduce a lot of innovative dishes to the menu and all. This restaurant is small and cozy with around 7-8 tables with a total sitting capacity of 40 people. This is an old restaurant who has kept them self-updated with latest food trends and drinks. The Ambiance of the restaurant is also smile and plan with nothing much in designs.

The first dish I tried was Aloo Nazakat. This is a small appetizer with a good burst of flavors. It’s a small potato cut in half which is marinated with a spicy marination. Then it is topped with cheeses later baked in grill. I liked this dish mainly because of it size. I would say its like a small boom of flavors. I would recommend you to try this dish and pair it with a sweet mocktail.

The second dish was The Corn Cheese Kurkure. This is a very good veg starters and I would go for this dish over many non-veg starters. This is a crispy dish with a very creamy filling. The inner filling is made up of palak paste mixed with cheese and corn, which is wrapped around spring roll wrap and the entire thing is deep fried until golden brown. This dish is served in shot glasses filled in green chutney and garnished with cheese. You can eat this dish like a finger sticks and its really enjoyable dish.

The Next dish was the Falafal Pocket. This is a middle eastern dish which is prepared very nicely by the restaurant. Basically what this dish is a fluffy form of pita bread which is stuffed with a creamy salad. This restaurant fills the bread with very little salad and serves the rest as side dish so as to fill it more as per your individual needs. They also serve Humus sauce which is prepared by their chef to go along with this dish. The texture of the dish is very tempting wanting you to fill it with more of the salad. If you want something new to eat go for this dish.

Then I went for the Main course in which the first was Panner in Coriander Sauce. This was a nice pan Asian dish prepared with delicate sauce. The Texture of the dish was dark and thick whereas the aroma was very light on the nose. This is a stirred fried dish which is cooked along with spring onion , scallops and herbs. The panner is soft and tender and well submersed in the flavor of the Coriander sauce. A must try dish along with some drink.

Next up was the Dunger Panner Biriyani. This dish was more on presentation then its taste. The texture of the dish was rich and the aroma was very strong everyone in the hotel could smell the dish as it comes to your table.  The dish is mixed with a creamy panners and aromatic rice. This dish is best suited to have it along with a group of people at the end.

The last dish was the Desert i.e. Gulab Jamun Cheese Cake. The cake is exactly as it sounds it to be. This is a cheese cake filled with Gulab Jamun throughout. The cake is light with a crummy base and filled with lots of Gulab Jamun. I really liked this dish and ended up eating 2 of it. I recommend you to try this dish for sure

featured_reviews.review_text:
Some restaurants impress with extravagance; others win you over with comfort, consistency, and food that simply hits the right notes. Bayleaf Cafe, Juhu, falls into the latter category.

From the moment we walked in, the warm ambience set the tone for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. The space strikes a nice balance between casual and inviting, making it ideal for an easy lunch, a coffee catch-up, or a leisurely dinner.

While everything we tried was enjoyable, the undisputed star of the table was the Pink Sauce Pasta. Rich, creamy, and beautifully balanced, it brought together the tanginess of tomato and the smoothness of a cream sauce in perfect harmony. Comfort food at its finest, and easily a dish worth returning for.

Good food, a pleasant atmosphere, and an experience that leaves you satisfied rather than rushed—Bayleaf Cafe delivered on all fronts. If you're in Juhu and looking for a relaxed dining spot, this cafe is well worth a visit. And whatever you order, don't leave without trying the Pink Sauce Pasta.

featured_reviews.name: Bipin Vora
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Vibrant Spot with a Kick: Blabber Juhu

​If you’re looking for a spot in Juhu that nails the "Instagrammable" aesthetic without sacrificing the quality of the meal, Blabber All Day is definitely worth a visit. Here is a breakdown of the experience:

​The Ambience
​The decor is easily the highlight. It’s elegant, whimsical, and filled with soft pastel hues and floral accents. Whether you’re looking for a brunch spot with friends or a cozy corner for a date, the atmosphere feels upscale yet welcoming. It’s one of those rare places where the lighting actually does you favors!

​The Food & Drink
​The menu is diverse, offering a great mix of global cuisines. The presentation is top-tier—everything from the cocktails to the dim sum arrives looking like a work of art.

​A Note on the Palate
​The food is undeniably high-quality, though it’s worth noting that the kitchen leans toward a bolder, spicier flavor profile.

​The Pro: The spices are fresh and aromatic, giving the dishes a real "zing" that stands out.
​The Caution: If you have a lower spice tolerance, you might find some dishes a bit intense.

​Tip: Don't hesitate to ask the servers to dial back the heat when you order; they are quite accommodating! Pairing your meal with one of their signature mocktails or shakes also helps balance out the fire.

Overall, Blabber Juhu is definitely worth a visit. Valet parking is available as well.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Blabber All Day recently and had a great experience overall! One of the major plus points is their valet parking facility, which makes things so much easier in a busy area like this.

We had a reservation via Zomato, and thankfully we did—because the place was fully packed! Booking in advance really helped us avoid the wait.

Once seated, the service was very attentive. A modern touch I appreciated was that there’s no physical menu—each table has a QR code you can scan to order directly, including for cocktails, appetizers, and mains. Another thoughtful feature is the “ring for service” button on each table, which alerts the staff directly instead of having to call them over repeatedly—very convenient!

The ambience is chic and aesthetic, with dim lighting and a peaceful vibe, perfect for a relaxed evening.

Here’s what we ordered:
•	Cheesy Stuffed Mushrooms – Juicy with mild, flavorful stuffing. A good start.
•	Crackling Rolls (Sushi) – Absolutely mind-blowing! So good that we reordered.
•	Edamame Truffle Dim Sum – Wasn’t a fan of this one. It looked good but lacked the punch.
•	Berry Smoke Cocktail – Great presentation and a refreshing mix of berries and herbs.
•	Spaghetti Aglio Olio with Pepperoni – Taste was decent, but it was on the drier side.

The staff was friendly and efficient, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable. I’d definitely recommend this place for a date night, an evening out with friends, family get-togethers, or even colleague dinners.

Tip: Make a reservation in advance to avoid waiting, and if you’re booking via Zomato, you can also avail 20% off when you pay through the app.

We were planning to visit JW Mariott at Juhu as it has a reputation of having really good ambience. The fireballs that greet you at the gate and more at pool side, everything screams luxury. The dessert section was overwhelming with icecreams, pastries and Indian Sweets like Rasmalai, Kaju roll, etc. It was all very good. However I would ask them to avoid multiple cakes and give some variety like Jalebi, cupcakes, eclair, etc.

On service front, it was amazing with very attentive and cheerful staff who caters to every need. Considering the cost, I would not recommend the buffet, but you can definitely come to dine. Best suited for evening with a good view of the pool.

featured_reviews.name: Ameen Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience here is truly great and has always been a highlight 🌟. I’ve been visiting this restaurant 2-3 times a year for the last 5-7 years, and earlier, the taste they delivered was gold. Back then, they really tried to include everything in their buffet, and the dessert section used to be huge and impressive 🍰🍮.

Now, let’s talk about the breakfast buffet—it’s pretty standard, similar to what you’d find at any 5-star continental breakfast 🍳🥐. They do include a few Indian dishes, but honestly, breakfast here has never excited me since the beginning.

As for dinner, it used to be something I truly looked forward to because of how flavourful and varied the food was 🍽️. However, over the last 2-3 visits, it feels like something is always off—sometimes it’s the salt, sometimes it’s the flavours. The food feels same-same now, and perhaps I’ve become fed up of eating the same dishes repeatedly. There’s nothing new or exciting anymore, and the taste is not extraordinary enough to crave anything specific. I used to love the pizza here; it was one of my favorites. But lately, the taste has literally deteriorated 😞. It’s just not the same anymore, and it’s disappointing to see the quality drop. Hope they bring back the original flavors they were known for.

That said, this place still shines for its ambience ✨, and for newcomers, it might still feel impressive and worth the visit. But for me, my interest in visiting Lotus Cafe is slowly fading away 😕. I guess it’s a matter of having it too many times.

Still, for the overall experience, I’d rate it 4 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Radha Krishna Veg Restaurant is a great spot for simple, comforting Maharashtrian food. We ordered misal pav, batata vada, and puri bhaji, and everything was fresh, tasty, and well prepared. The misal had a good balance of spice, the batata vada was crisp, and the puri bhaji was satisfying and filling. The total bill came to around ₹800, which felt reasonable for the quantity and quality.

The ambience is simple and clean, with a calm, no-frills setup that suits a traditional vegetarian restaurant. It has a homely, comfortable feel, making it ideal for families and casual dining. The seating is basic but well maintained, and the overall atmosphere is peaceful and welcoming, letting the food remain the main highlight.

Overall, a good place for a wholesome vegetarian meal.

featured_reviews.name: ANIL ZALA
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Govinda’s Bistro, located inside the serene ISKCON Juhu Temple, and the experience was truly delightful from start to finish. The calm, spiritual ambiance of the temple sets the perfect tone for a soulful meal, making it much more than just a restaurant visit.

What makes Govinda’s Bistro stand out is its pure vegetarian, satvik food prepared without onion and garlic, yet packed with incredible flavor. We sampled a wide variety of dishes, and every single one exceeded our expectations.

The lotus stem dish was beautifully cooked perfectly tender with a satisfying crunch, well-seasoned, and full of earthy flavors. The ramen was comforting and aromatic, with a well-balanced broth and thoughtfully cooked vegetables, proving that even global cuisines can shine without onion and garlic.

The pizza was another highlight, with a crisp base, generous toppings, and a rich, cheesy flavor that didn’t feel heavy. The pasta was creamy and indulgent, yet light on the palate, showing excellent balance in seasoning and texture. The Thai curry with basil rice was absolutely delicious—the curry was fragrant, mildly spiced, and creamy, pairing perfectly with the aromatic basil rice.

To end the meal on a sweet note, we had the gulkand ice cream, which was refreshing, unique, and incredibly soothing. Its delicate rose flavors made it the perfect dessert to round off such a satisfying meal.

Overall, Govinda’s Bistro delivers exceptional taste, variety, and quality, proving that food made without onion and garlic can still be rich, flavorful, and memorable. Combined with the peaceful temple surroundings and wholesome ingredients, this place offers a truly nourishing dining experience for both the body and the soul. Highly recommended for anyone looking for delicious vegetarian food with a spiritual touch. 🌿🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Amey M
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a Satvic restaurant that serves food on a thali as well as à la carte basis. All items are onion- and garlic-free, yet the taste competes well with many non-Satvic restaurants. The ambience is pleasant, noise-free, and parking is available on a pay-and-park basis. Their menu changes daily, which is a nice touch.

They offer 2 salads, 4 starters, 4 vegetables, 3 types of rice, pasta, 2 dals, 4 flavours of welcome drinks, 3 sweets, and 2 desserts. The quality and quantity are good.

However, consistency in taste is an issue. Don’t expect the same flavour every day—especially the dal tadka, which often tastes like simple plain dal. Since the food is served buffet-style, you may not get the full dining experience you expect.

It seems they use soda in many items, and some dishes share the same gravy—for example, pasta and a couple of vegetables having a similar base. They also serve more liquid items, possibly to control quantity. Serving multiple items on small plates can also reduce the overall satisfaction.

Overall, the variety is impressive, the ambience is good, and the food is decent—but consistency and preparation style could be improved.

Had a wonderful dining experience at Tanatan! The vibrant ambiance, beautiful interiors, and lively live music created the perfect atmosphere for a fun evening out. The energy of the place was amazing, making it an ideal spot to unwind with friends and family.

We tried quite a few dishes, and every item impressed us with its presentation and flavors:
🥤 Popcorn Shake
🍹 Tarbooz Without Booz
🍗 Banjara Murg Tikka
🌶️ Zafrani Tangdi
🥗 Non Veg Dilli Ki Gali
🍛 Chicken Biryani

The Banjara Murg Tikka and Zafrani Tangdi were perfectly cooked and packed with flavor. The Chicken Biryani was aromatic and satisfying, while the Gulkand Cheese Cake was a unique and delicious way to end the meal. The mocktails were refreshing and complemented the food really well.

The service was prompt, the ambiance was lively, and the live music elevated the entire experience. A perfect combination of great food, great vibes, and great hospitality. Looking forward to visiting again!

Highly recommended for anyone looking for delicious North Indian food, refreshing drinks, and a fantastic ambiance in Juhu. ❤️✨

featured_reviews.name: The Beekeeper
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Tanatan near Juhu Beach on Christmas Eve for lunch. The first thing that stands out about the place is its beautiful interiors — they are quite impressive and give off a royal, grand kind of vibe. The ambience definitely adds to the overall dining experience. They also had live music during the daytime, which created a pleasant and lively atmosphere.

The service, however, was average. The staff was polite, but the food preparation and service took longer than expected, so you might have to wait a bit for your order to arrive at the table.

In terms of food, I ordered the tandoori chicken. Unfortunately, it wasn’t the best experience. The chicken was slightly burnt on the sides and, considering the price, the portion size and quality didn’t really justify the cost. The place felt a bit on the expensive side overall.

I’m rating this place 3 stars mainly because of the ambience and the overall experience the restaurant offers. However, the food quality and pricing could definitely be improved to match the premium feel of the place.

featured_reviews.name: Dheeraj Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful dining experience here. The ambience is beautiful with warm interiors, comfortable seating, and live music that made the evening even more enjoyable. We started with the Peeli Mirch Ke Wings and Kozhi Ghee Roast, both packed with flavour and cooked perfectly. The wings had the right balance of spice, while the ghee roast was rich and aromatic.
For the mains, the Sunny Side Up Appam with Chicken Sukhna was a unique combination and easily my favourite dish of the night. The Chicken Tikka Biryani was flavourful with tender pieces of chicken and well-cooked rice. Paired everything with the refreshing Thanda Teekha Mocktail and ended on a sweet note with the indulgent Killer KitKat Freakshake. Great food, great vibe, and excellent service. Highly recommended!

Had a wonderful dining experience at Tanatan Juhu, especially with their limited-time Mango Menu, which is currently live. We started with the Mango Colada, a refreshing tropical drink with the perfect balance of sweetness and mango flavor. For dessert, the fresh mango chunks served with vanilla ice cream were simple yet incredibly satisfying, making the most of the season's best fruit.

Among the starters, the Hara Bhara Tikke stood out with its crisp exterior and flavorful, well-seasoned filling. The Paneer Tikka was equally impressive—soft, smoky, and marinated beautifully with rich spices. For the main course, we opted for the biryani, which was aromatic, flavorful, and cooked to perfection with well-balanced spices.

The food, presentation, and overall ambiance made for a memorable meal. The seasonal mango offerings added a unique touch to the experience. A great spot for enjoying delicious food and innovative seasonal specials in a vibrant setting.

featured_reviews.name: Avni Barai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had such a lovely dinner at Tanatan, Juhu last night with friends! The vibe was great, but the food honestly stole the show.

We started with the Avocado Thecha—a super unique twist with just the right balance of creamy and spicy. The Zucchini Paneer Roll was another standout, really fresh and flavourful.

The Firangi Nuska was interesting and well-executed, and the Tandoori Butter Roti paired perfectly with the comforting Dal Khichdi—simple, but done so well.

For drinks, Anar Ka Pyaar was refreshing and not overly sweet. And desserts were a total highlight—Killer Kit Kat was indulgent and fun, while the Rajasthani Ghevar added a nice traditional touch to end the meal.

Overall, a great mix of innovative and comforting dishes. Definitely a place I’d come back to!

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Hatiskar
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an amazing dining experience at Tanatan where the ambience instantly sets the mood with classy interiors, warm lighting, and soothing live music that makes the evening feel special and lively at the same time. We started with the Bhuna Chaap which was smoky, flavorful, and perfectly cooked with tender texture in every bite. The Murg Bharwaan Lahori was rich and indulgent with delicious stuffing and a creamy gravy that had bold authentic flavors. The Lucknowi Nihari stood out with its deep aromatic taste and slow cooked meat that was extremely soft and full of spices. The Chicken Biryani was fragrant and well layered with balanced flavors and juicy chicken pieces that made it very satisfying. Cheese Garlic Naan was soft, buttery, and generously filled with cheese, pairing beautifully with the gravies. The cocktails Penicillin and South Side were refreshing and well crafted, one offering smoky citrus notes and the other giving a light minty freshness that complemented the food perfectly. We ended the meal with Rasgulla Tiramisu which was a unique fusion dessert combining soft rasgulla with creamy tiramisu layers creating a delightful balance of flavors. Overall the food quality, presentation, service, and live music made it a complete and memorable experience.

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & First Impression
Thyme & Whisk is located at a prime spot, which gives it great potential and makes it easily accessible. Considering the location, the café has a lot of scope to stand out even more with the right upgrades.

Ambience & Interior
The overall vibe was okay, but the interior felt a bit outdated. The café would truly benefit from a proper renovation to give it a fresher, more modern look that matches its prime location. The artificial trees placed inside didn’t quite work for me—the pink and purple tones felt off. Natural green shades would have blended much better and enhanced the overall ambience.

Food Experience
The food was average and just okayish. It wasn’t bad, but it didn’t particularly stand out either. With some refinement in flavors and presentation, the food experience could definitely be elevated.

Staff & Service
The highlight of my visit was the staff. They were extremely friendly, polite, and attentive throughout. Their warm service genuinely made the experience more pleasant and left a positive impression.

Final Verdict
Thyme & Whisk has strong potential because of its prime location and great staff. With a fresh renovation, improved interior choices, and some upgrades to the food, this café could easily transform into a much more appealing spot. The hospitality, however, was truly commendable.

featured_reviews.name: Vidhi Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Frankly I was confused about how I would rate my experience here. We have been to thyme and whisk (Juhu) many times. But we decided to visit worli outlet first time. We ordered triple schezwan for main course along with another dish. Usually triple schezwan is served with rice, noodles and Manchurian balls. So with that in mind we ordered it. But when our order arrived , Manchurian balls were missing. So we asked the staff about it and they said they don't serve triple schezwan with Manchurian balls here. We called the person who had placed the order Mr. Chetan. A very kind, polite and professional person. He said repeated what the other staff member said. But I insisted that it is generally served with the dish. He kindly offered to give us few Manchurian balls with the dish as we were not informed prior about it. But warned us that next time they won't. We accepted and were about to move on when suddenly the manager Mr. Vishal came and told us that this is what we serve here and this is what you will get. It must be happening in other places but here we don't do it and that is it. There is nothing wrong with both the things. And it might not affect people in general but I liked the way Mr. Chetan handled it. It's not about giving it or not. It is about hospitality. Restaurants comes under hospitality and the better you serve your customers the more they will prefer to come at your place. I hope the higher ups will appreciate a man like Mr. Chetan in their restaurant because such people makes a business grow. All the best Mr. Chetan really appreciate your hospitality and kindness because in a difficult situation, persons true talent is shown.

featured_reviews.name: chirag shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Service was so so, food was average, but the worst part of this so-called fine dining experience was seeing a mouse roaming inside the restaurant. Even after informing the manager, he was least bothered to check, and behaved as if it was completely normal.

If this is what you call fine dining, then what’s the difference between this place and a local Irani café? Why charge ₹1,500–₹2,000 per person when basic hygiene is not maintained?

On top of that, it’s extremely noisy — the only good thing here is the ambience, and that alone is not worth risking our health.

To make matters worse, the manager didn’t even offer an apology. This was an extremely disappointing experience — my evening was ruined, my money wasted, and it caused unnecessary stress. I will never visit here again and strongly advise others to avoid this place.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Walked out before ordering due to incredibly high-friction tech policies and poor hospitality practices.
​First, there is absolutely no physical menu. Instead of a standard QR code that links to a simple website or PDF, the qr code insisted that guests must send a message on WhatsApp just to request access to the menu. There is zero technical or safety justification for this anymore; it feels entirely like a forced data-collection tactic to harvest verified phone numbers for future marketing spam.
​To make matters worse, when we asked for standard filtered water, we were told they "don't have it" and were forced to buy bottled water. For an upscale or mainstream establishment, claiming a commercial kitchen doesn't have safe, potable filtered water is highly questionable and is a transparent tactic to pad the bill.
​Hospitality should be about welcoming guests, not extracting their personal data and forcing upsells before they've even ordered food. Glad we chose to leave and take our business elsewhere. Downright disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Yati Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic, no-frills South Indian food in Juhu, Sri Annapoorna Cafe is an absolute gem. The menu is refreshingly simple, but every item delivers on taste, quality, and authenticity.

The sambhar is rich, perfectly spiced, and feels like it’s straight out of a traditional South Indian kitchen. The benne podi masala dosa is a standout—crispy on the outside, generously layered with butter, and packed with flavorful podi that hits just right.

The idli with rasam is comfort in a plate—soft, fluffy idlis paired with a tangy, soul-warming rasam that you’ll want to keep sipping. And the vada? Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and absolutely worth the hype.

What really sets this place apart is how it sticks to its roots—no unnecessary gimmicks, just honest, traditional flavors done right. Add to that the pocket-friendly pricing, and you’ve got a spot that’s truly worth every rupee.

Simple menu, authentic taste, and consistently good food—definitely a must-visit for South Indian lovers.

featured_reviews.review_text: Fantastic North Indian Feast at Copper Chimney, Juhu. The mixed grill was a star, juicy and smoky with an array of chutneys that added zesty punches of flavor. featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
I attended the currently ongoing  "Phulkari" event by Copper chimney a meticulously crafted, flavourful and colorful menu inspired by Phulkari. Phulkari, after all, is more than just an art; it symbolizes tradition, joy, and togetherness....the very spirit of Diwali.

Foods on the menu that are a must try-
✨ Rose rumali roti with a creamy and flavourful walnut malai dip- A crisp rumali roti with subtle hints of rose teams with a creamy mellow walnutty dip.
✨ Chukandar Tikki with Missi Roti: The absolute melt in the mouth " Chukandar Tikki" with Missi Roti made me think....Who knew beetroot could taste so good 😅
✨Tandoori Pineapple- Smoky, spiced and my personal favourite.(....yes, I am biased when it comes to spiced pineapple😅)

And if you have a sweet tooth....

✨ Mava gujiya: A classic and must have.
✨ Badam halwa with malai ice cream: Rich, creamy and  definitely not for the faint hearted 😅

Drinks:
✨ Phoolkari- A subtle and soothing drink inspired by Bagh phulkari
✨ Anar Da Bagh- Another beautifully crafted drink inspired by Bagh Phulkari

Overall, Phulkari by Copper Chimney feels like a cultural celebration on a plate through flavor, color, and creativity.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute is one of the best Middle Eastern restaurants if you are looking for authentic flavours, beautiful presentation, and a relaxed dining experience. The food arrives as a visual treat, and every dish feels thoughtfully prepared with a balance of spices and textures that reflect Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine.

We started with refreshing mocktails like the Green Avocado and the Salted Caramel Baklava Sheikh, followed by the classic Bayroute Muhammara — smoky, nutty, and addictive. The Shrimp Provencal was juicy and perfectly spiced, while the Chelow Kebab with rice stood out for its simplicity and flavour. The Moroccan Lemon Olive Chicken was tender, aromatic, and comforting.

To end the meal, the Chocolate Kunafa was crispy, gooey, and indulgent. The warm lighting, elegant interiors, and calm ambience make Bayroute ideal for date nights, family dinners, or relaxed evenings with friends. If you are searching for a premium Middle Eastern dining experience, Bayroute is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: shravan saroj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute in Juhu offers a spectacular culinary journey across the Middle East. The ambiance is luxurious and elegant, making it perfect for a special occasion.
They specialize in authentic Turkish, Lebanese, and Mediterranean cuisine. Their menu features a delightful array of classics, all prepared with finesse.
A must-try is the signature hummus—creamy and flavorful—along with the perfectly flaky Baklava. The 'Egyptian Photo' cocktail is highly popular for its unique, Instagram-worthy presentation.
While the food quality and presentation are exceptional, the service can sometimes be a little slow. Despite this, the attentive and polite staff ensure a pleasant dining experience. It remains a top recommendation for those seeking a truly authentic and high-end taste of the Levant in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Vipasha Pillai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dinner at Bayroute with my mom recently was a fantastic experience, especially since it was our first visit here. The restaurant impressed us instantly with its tasteful interiors and calming ambience, making it ideal for a relaxed dinner. The service complemented the setting beautifully. Thanks to Shadab, who was taking care of our table. He was attentive and helped us with spot-on recommendations.
.
Here's everything we tried (Highly Recommend):
1. Sumac De-light: A beautifully balanced cocktail with half vodka and half gin. It was refreshing and presented beautifully in a glass dome with smoke
2. Rehan: A light and incredibly refreshing mocktail
3. Harissa Chicken Kebab: Chicken was grilled to absolute perfection and served with a unique cream cheese dip
4. Chicken Afrikaan: A signature Pide (Turkish flatbread) dish. It was flavourful and super comforting with just the right amount of spices and chicken chunks
5. Lavash Crust Chicken Kabsa: Soo loved this! It's an aromatic spiced rice dish paired with tender chicken and a crisp lavash layer that added great texture to the dish
6. Baklava: Finally, ended our meal with their signature dessert that was crisp, nutty and indulgently sweet
.
Overall, the food stood out for its depth of flavour with Middle Eastern & Mediterranean influences coming through beautifully in every dish. Everything was well-balanced, well-presented and soo delicious. A special mention for the restaurant manager, Mr. Gautam, whose warm and gracious hospitality added a personal touch to our dining experience 😊
.
Bayroute delivers on every front, be it ambience, food, drinks and service. It's worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: Indica Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute is a stunning Middle Eastern restaurant that offers a perfect blend of elegance, comfort, and cultural charm. The moment you step in, the ambiance draws you in with its warm tones, tasteful interiors, and thoughtfully designed spaces that feel both inviting and premium.
The restaurant is spacious with comfortable seating, making it ideal for families, group gatherings, and even intimate date nights. The décor reflects Middle Eastern aesthetics beautifully—subtle, classy, and immersive without being overwhelming.
What truly enhances the experience is the hospitality. The staff is polite, attentive, and extremely accommodating, ensuring everything runs smoothly while making guests feel genuinely welcome. The overall vibe of the restaurant is relaxed yet lively, allowing you to enjoy conversations without any rush.
Bayroute is more than just a restaurant—it’s a place where ambiance, service, and experience come together effortlessly. A great choice for those looking to enjoy a refined dining atmosphere with an international touch.
Highly recommended for anyone seeking a memorable restaurant experience.

featured_reviews.name: Shadab Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”
